title: TerraGuard NER
context: Smart India Hackathon 2026 (SIH26001, MDoNER), Team Aaroh, team lead
summary: A software-only landslide early warning platform for India's North East. It needs no physical sensors and aims to give district authorities and communities earlier warning.
highlights: Built a hybrid risk engine: a rule-based rainfall threshold baseline designed to take an ML layer later
Built a live GIS dashboard across 7 West Kameng zones with rainfall trend charts, a manual rainfall slider, and a rainfall spike simulation
Built a cross-device emergency buzzer using Supabase Realtime, with a siren and full-screen alert on HIGH-risk transitions

title: Ocean Arcade
summary: A self-contained multiplayer game console on one ESP32. Players join its WiFi hotspot and play browser games together, with no internet, app, or server needed.
highlights: Built a captive portal that opens the game hub on connect, with real-time play over a WebSocket relay on the ESP32
Fixed async TCP library conflicts by switching to RPAsyncTCP
Fixed blank captive portal pages across devices by using absolute URLs; added AP+STA mode with mDNS at oceanarcade.local

title: FitCore
summary: A gym management app built to sell white-label to gyms in Guntur district, for a one-time setup fee plus optional monthly maintenance.
highlights: Reached a working Android APK after setting up the full build pipeline
Fixed a GoRouter redirect loop with a refresh notifier and corrected route constants
Removed hardcoded mock IDs and added the missing INTERNET permission to the Android manifest

title: Attendance Tracker
summary: An Android app that tracks attendance per subject and shows how many more classes you need to stay above the limit.
highlights: Lets students import a timetable from a photo and import past attendance from XLS sheets
Warns about low attendance per subject, and handles extra Saturdays and suspended hours in the calendar
Designed to be fast and lightweight

title: DHARA
summary: An AI-powered precision agriculture platform for farmers in India. ESP32 sensors feed a backend pipeline that produces farming recommendations in a mobile app.
highlights: Expanded the backend from 9 to 17 API endpoints and wired the sensor-to-recommendation pipeline into the API layer, verified with real payloads
Built the Flutter app flows: phone and OTP auth, farm onboarding, BLE and manual-code device pairing, and an 8-metric dashboard
Working on the current blocker: writing Wi-Fi and backend credentials to the ESP32 with NVS provisioning

title: MARCO AI
summary: A personal AI voice assistant and developer workspace with a 3D control panel and a browser-based code editor.
highlights: Built the AI brain on Groq's llama-3.3-70b with a local Ollama fallback when offline
Built a WebSocket server that syncs voice state and transcription with the frontend, plus a Three.js control panel
Added a code execution engine supporting 25+ languages and integrations for web search, Gmail, Spotify/YouTube, and reminders

title: SwarmMind
summary: A multi-agent platform that analyses ideas through several AI agents and returns structured insight. It is a rebranded fork of the MiroFish frontend, plus a standalone React frontend.
highlights: Built a standalone frontend in React, TypeScript, and Vite
Rebranded the MiroFish Vue 3 frontend: full English translation, a prompt-only input flow, and a new agent detail side panel
Scoped changes to the frontend only, with no backend or architecture changes, and fixed polling lifecycle issues across four views

title: SignBridge
summary: A privacy-first, client-side Indian Sign Language phrase assistant. Recognition runs in the browser.
highlights: Built a 173-dimension kinematic joint-angle feature system with z-score standardization and per-phrase acceptance thresholds
Added LB_Keogh pruning for about a 46x speedup in matching, and a sentence accumulation mode
Designing an air-writing mode with a two-hand gesture interface; tool locking is still unreliable

title: ESP32 CSI Presence
summary: A privacy-preserving presence and movement system on a single ESP32, with no extra sensors. It uses Wi-Fi channel data (CSI) to detect people, movement, and breathing.
highlights: Detects movement and breathing from live Wi-Fi CSI data, and tracks nearby devices through probe request and BLE advertisement sniffing
Hosts a live dashboard on the ESP32 showing the CSI graph and device list, with active devices highlighted
Restarting the dashboard from scratch; the next version adds a floor-plan map with live human movement

title: Smart Fan
summary: An IoT fan that adjusts its operation based on environmental conditions, using sensor readings and embedded control.
highlights: Integrates sensors with an ESP32 to control the fan automatically
Demonstrates embedded system control driven by environmental data
